filename: Differentiable modelling to unify machine learning and physical models for geosciences.pdf
title: Differentiable modelling to unify machine learning and physical models for geosciences
parameterization_target: Hydrological parameters and process relations (e.g. soil moisture-runoff relations, hydraulic conductivity, Manning roughness, photosynthesis)
host_model: HBV, VIC, EXP-HYDRO, Richards equation solvers
testbed_rationale: This paper is a Perspective/Review synthesis paper presenting conceptual and methodological frameworks for differentiable modelling; it synthesizes existing literature and figures from previously published work rather than introducing a new standalone open dataset/benchmark.
pain_points: Computational expense and GPU memory constraints for automatic differentiation through numerical iterative/PDE solvers
Equifinality and process non-uniqueness (equifinality) when learning unknown subcomponents
Heterogeneous numerical operations which are difficult to parallelize and optimize on GPUs compared to standard matrix multiplications
Need to balance forward- and backward-mode automatic differentiation versus adjoint equations
extraction_notes: This is a Perspective article published in Nature Reviews Earth & Environment discussing differentiable modelling across geosciences (primarily hydrological modeling examples). It surveys previous published works by the authors and others (e.g. Feng et al. 2022, Tsai et al. 2021, Tartakovsky et al. 2020).
